evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.261: versūs multōs ūnō spīritū prōnūntiāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also to announce and to deliver a speech or a verdict; the way one says a word is prōnūntiātiō (Quintilian).

phrases.english: to pronounce a vowel short or long

phrases.latin: Quōmodo hoc verbum prōnūntiātur? Prīmane syllaba longa est an brevis?
phrases.english: How is this word pronounced? Is the first syllable long or short?

phrases.latin: His igitur assentimus, quī «putum» esse dīcunt ā «putandō» dictum et ob eam causam prīmā syllabā brevī prōnūntiant, nōn longā
phrases.english: So we agree with those who say that putum comes from putare, and therefore pronounce the first syllable short, not long

phrases.latin: Is «affatim» ut «admodum» prīmā acūtā, nōn mediā, prōnūntiābat atque ita veterēs locūtōs cēnsēbat.
phrases.english: He pronounced affatim, like admodum, with the accent on the first syllable, not the middle one, and believed the ancients spoke so.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 31, 366.
